PullRequest.Title: git: remove two IGitService fallbacks that never find anything new
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

## Why

This is the first stage of deprecating the core `IGitService`, which reaches the Git extension through an extension-host bridge and waits up to 10 seconds for it to register. Two callers can stop using `IGitService` without a replacement, because their fallbacks never return anything new.

## What changed

- **Delegation picker** (`delegationSessionPickerActionItem.ts`). It asked `IGitService` for repositories only in the Agents window, when the picker delegate had no `hasGitRepository` callback. The only menu entry for this picker is hidden in the Agents window by `IsSessionsWindowContext.negate()`, so that fallback never runs. The picker now uses only the delegate's `hasGitRepository` callback.
- **Onboarding V3 prompt** (`newSessionViewV3Prompt.ts`). Its last step asked the Git extension for remotes, but it runs only after the prompt has parsed the same `.git/config` itself. The Git extension reads remotes from that file too, so the step could not find a remote the parse missed. The step and the `IGitService` constructor parameter are removed.

## Tests

The local and GitHub Enterprise remote tests in `newSessionViewV3Prompt.test.ts` now read the remote from a `.git/config` file in an in-memory file service, instead of from a mocked `IGitService`. They still cover the remote lookup path.

## How to test

```sh
npm run typecheck-client
npm run transpile-client
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/onboardingTours/test/browser/newSessionViewV3Prompt.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/delegationSessionPickerActionItem.test.ts
```

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- The two test files: 38 passing.
- `npm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.

No live run. The delegation fallback cannot run, and the unit tests cover the onboarding path.

## Next stages

Each remaining caller (automation branch picker, customization commits, chat Issue and Pull Request context, and the editor cloud sandbox) needs `ILocalGitService` to gain a web implementation and new operations first. Each will land in its own PR, followed by the deletion of `IGitService` and the bridge.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Repository-resolution misses unnecessarily awaited IGitService.openRepository before returning noRepository. GitService waits on a barrier that opens at delegate registration or 10 seconds after service construction. A registered delegate instead queues every open globally and crosses extension-host IPC; its cold path activates the Git extension and probes the directory. This was one extra open per unresolved primary-folder lookup, not per workspace folder or issue.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: During early onboarding with an unsupported/missing GitHub remote and no applicable Agent Host metadata wait (for example, an Enterprise account selecting a public GitHub repository), prompt insertion/final option resolution could wait for the remaining Git-service registration barrier or the 10-second overall lookup timeout, despite having no useful repository to discover. With a registered delegate, the miss also incurred serialized IPC/probing.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: After unchanged session metadata, URI, .git/config, and applicable Agent Host metadata checks fail, return undefined directly; remove the Git-service dependency and redundant awaited extension lookup.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Deleted base line 961 awaited _gitService.openRepository after local config resolution failed; added head lines 958-959 now return undefined immediately. run() awaits _resolveGitHubPromptWithFallback before animatePrompt (299-306); _resolveGitHubPrompt awaits repository resolution (661-667). Both GitHub prompt modes have a 10-second outer race (41, 432-459, 616-639). GitService.openRepository waits on AutoOpenBarrier(10_000) (git/browser/gitService.ts:20,47-58). MainThreadGitExtensionService.openRepository globally sequences and unconditionally calls $openRepository (102-126); extHostGitExtensionService.ts:207-214,373-392 activates the Git API and calls its openRepository. Enterprise mode bypasses Agent Host waiting (prompt.ts:941), establishing a reachable miss even for an Agent Host draft. Blame of the removed await identifies the introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore the Agents window and register the V3 onboarding contribution.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AfterRestored constructs the contribution, trigger, and prompt runner and registers the tour. Repository and GitHub lookups run only when the tour reaches its prompt step; construction itself does not await them.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One contribution per window; one eligible tour trigger, with prompt-option refreshes owned by the composer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous contribution construction followed by existing observable-triggered onboarding execution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Shared services remain singleton-owned. Removing IGitService injection avoids requesting that dependency from these constructors; no new cache or retained collection is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and AfterRestored registration were inspected; only the Git dependency and argument are removed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether another consumer has already instantiated GitService determines any dependency-construction saving.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced startup work or retention. Remaining initialization and service dependencies are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct, render, and open the delegation picker in an existing chat.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Toolbar creation builds the picker; opening it synchronously evaluates visibility and enablement. Cloud repository checking still invokes the same delegate callback where supplied.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A bounded provider list per picker evaluation. The default callback scans current in-memory SCM repositories, unchanged from before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI evaluation. No new subprocess, filesystem, IPC, database, or network call is introduced by replacing the helper with the optional callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both toolbar factories already supply hasGitRepository. The removed fallback read the Git bridge's existing in-memory repository iterable, not an IPC discovery operation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both chatInputPart factories and hasWorkspaceScmRepository were inspected; the only production menu entry is guarded by IsSessionsWindowContext.negate().
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom delegates and test-only Sessions-window picker instances can omit the callback, but the change then removes work rather than adding it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Removing the fallback does not increase callback frequency, rendering work, or repository discovery; missing-callback behavior is not a performance finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve onboarding prompts/options when the selected primary folder has no supported GitHub repository.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository resolution precedes GitHub lookup and, in githubPrompt mode, prompt insertion. Options mode publishes standard options before lookup, so initial usable options are off the lookup critical path, while final resolution still waits. Applicable non-Enterprise Agent Host metadata waiting remains unchanged; Enterprise mode bypasses that wait and reaches the removed fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sequentially stat ancestor .git entries and, if present, read .git/config or worktree gitdir/commondir metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only folders[0] is examined. At most 50 ancestor probes per resolution, ordinarily one probe plus a config read for a repository; worktrees add metadata reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same direct-config search ran before the Git-extension fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before concluding noRepository; unchanged total lookup timeout bounds user-visible resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the selected directory through $openRepository in the extension host, returning repository metadata/state when found.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one call per primary-folder resolution reaching the fallback when a delegate existed, including warm calls; now zero. No delegate meant barrier waiting but no IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fallback unconditionally requested openRepository after the existing checks failed; the PR removes that boundary from this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously awaited after direct resolution failed, globally sequenced behind other repository opens. A missing delegate could consume the remainder of the 10-second registration barrier; now this entire await is removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The removed cold extension fallback could activate Git and probe an uncached directory with git rev-parse --show-toplevel, followed by repository opening if applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when the delegate was absent, URI was not file, Git was disabled, or the exact repository was already open. Otherwise at least one directory-root probe for an uncached local path; now none from this caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold paths reached Git extension activation/probing; warm exact repositories avoided probing but still crossed IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously inside the awaited, globally serialized extension lookup; now absent from onboarding resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected primary directory per run/refresh, not every workspace folder. Refreshes can repeat misses; ancestor depth is capped at 50.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filesystem ancestry probes are serial. The removed bridge used a global Sequencer, not per-key parallelism. Existing Agent Host observable waiting and cancellation remain unchanged; prompt lookups have a 10-second outer race.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Direct-config resolution has no runner-level positive/negative cache. Previously Git API and repository objects could be warm, but bridge openRepository still queued and issued IPC on each fallback; failures were not coalesced into a cached onboarding result. Removal eliminates both cold and warm fallback calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted await, service barrier, global sequencer, extension API activation, and local Git root probe were traced. No timing measurements were inferred.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact delay depends on service age, delegate availability, Git activation state, directory contents, and whether the Enterprise/non-Agent-Host fallback is reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new regression; this removes a concrete latency mechanism. Its introducing commit was resolved by blame and recorded through report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Personalize onboarding from session/URI metadata or a supported local/Enterprise .git/config remote, including composer refresh and late Agent Host metadata.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Metadata/URI resolution returns immediately when available; otherwise config reads or existing cancellable Agent Host metadata waiting precede GitHub requests. githubPrompt waits for candidate selection before animation. Options mode renders standard options immediately and streams candidates, so review enrichment only delays review-specific refinement/final completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a supported remote from local repository configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for supported session/URI metadata; otherwise one bounded ancestor search for the primary directory, usually one stat and one config read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical config resolver already preceded the removed extension fallback and returned immediately on success.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before fetching personalized candidates; no placement or frequency change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch assigned issues and authored PR summaries, a grouped issue-linkage query, and eligible PR review-thread summaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two summary requests for one resolved repository, each limited to five results; zero or one grouped linkage request for up to five issues. P eligible PRs, at most five, each require one PR read and sequential thread-summary pages (up to 100). With one thread page each, the usual bound is 3+2P requests, not one linkage request per issue. Compatible concurrent identical reads can share transport work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful metadata/config paths already performed these exact requests with the same result caps, grouping, pagination, and scheduling; they never reached the removed fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Summary chains run independently; linkage follows issues and review pages follow PR reads. Existing per-stage deadlines and the 10-second total race bound personalization. Initial standard options do not wait for network.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One repository per selected primary folder, up to five issue and five PR summaries, eligible PR count P, thread-page count per PR, and composer refreshes. Workspace changes can restart the existing lookup loop within its total deadline.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two summary chains run concurrently; up to five eligible review lookups use Promise.all, with pages serialized within each lookup. Platform RequestQueue retains the existing limits: 12 global/host active requests, 10 per account, 8 per caller, with bounded admission and rate-limit backpressure. Option enrichment retains its existing priority.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new runner result cache. GitHubApiClient shares account-client acquisition and clears failed acquisition; transport coalesces compatible in-flight REST/GraphQL reads by account/request identity. Warm REST responses use ETag revalidation rather than eliminating all network calls; completed GraphQL reads are not an onboarding result cache. Config and negative repository outcomes still resolve per refresh as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: prompt call paths, fetcher limits/grouping, account-client sharing, transport coalescing/ETag behavior, and platform concurrency limits were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network latency, review-thread pagination, cache overlap, refresh frequency, and late metadata timing vary, but none is increased by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Production successful resolution paths and their expensive boundaries are unchanged. Updated tests replace finite mocked Git repository state with finite in-memory config reads, not production I/O.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all five changed files and every diff page. Traced contribution startup, both delegation-picker factories, repository successes/misses, asynchronous metadata, and downstream Git/GitHub boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue qualifies for report_finding. Recorded one proven removal of redundant awaited Git-extension fallback work as an internal regression fix. Static review; no runtime measurements.
